name: Bird of Paradise

chemicals.name: Gastrointestinal irritants
chemicals.description: The toxic principle is an unspecified gastrointestinal irritant. It causes mild digestive upset such as nausea, vomiting and diarrhea after ingestion.
chemicals.concentration_notes: The irritant effects are attributed mainly to the fruit and seeds.

treatments.name: Decontamination (Inducing Vomiting)
treatments.description: If the ingestion was recent, the veterinarian may administer medication to induce vomiting (emesis) to expel the plant material from the stomach before toxins are fully absorbed.
treatments.notes: This is a general protocol for plant poisoning to prevent further absorption of toxins. Sources emphasize that pet owners should not attempt to induce vomiting at home (e.g., using hydrogen peroxide) as it can cause injury; this must be done by a veterinary professional.

treatments.name: Fluid Therapy
treatments.description: The administration of intravenous (IV) fluids to maintain hydration and electrolyte balance.
treatments.notes: This is necessary to counteract dehydration caused by the gastrointestinal symptoms associated with Bird of Paradise ingestion, specifically vomiting and diarrhea. Fluid therapy also helps flush toxins from the body and supports kidney function.

treatments.name: Symptomatic Management and Monitoring
treatments.description: The use of medications to control nausea and close observation of the cat until the gastrointestinal signs resolve.
treatments.notes: Because the plant acts as a gastrointestinal irritant, care focuses on controlling nausea, vomiting and diarrhea; gastroprotectants may be used to soothe the digestive tract.

safetyNotes: Symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, mild diarrhea, and drowsiness are the most common signs; symptoms are typically self-limiting but unpleasant.
Fruit and seeds are the highest-risk parts: The fruit and seeds are the components most associated with toxicity and should be removed promptly if accessible.
Action: Monitor the cat and contact a vet if vomiting is persistent, or if the cat appears unusually lethargic after known or suspected ingestion.
description: Bird of Paradise (Strelitzia reginae and Strelitzia nicolai) is a popular ornamental plant known for its dramatic orange-and-blue flowers and large tropical foliage. It is mildly toxic to cats. The toxic principle is a gastrointestinal irritant, and the effects are attributed mainly to the fruit and seeds. While the toxicity level is low compared to many houseplants, ingestion can cause mild but unpleasant digestive upset, and signs typically resolve on their own. Most cases involve a curious cat chewing the fruit or seeds rather than the foliage.

symptoms.name: Nausea, Vomiting, and Diarrhea
symptoms.notes: These digestive issues are caused by the gastrointestinal irritant in the plant, attributed mainly to the fruit and seeds.

symptoms.name: Drowsiness (Lethargy)
symptoms.notes: This symptom is primarily associated with the ingestion of the seeds or fruit.
